unit.title: Engineering a Reliable Linear Regression Component
prerequisites: Comfort with vectors, matrices, derivatives, and asymptotic analysis
Ability to run Python unittest tests from a terminal
learning_objectives: Translate the mean-squared-error objective into a deterministic batch-gradient-descent implementation
Design and document a small prediction API with explicit validation and fitted-state contracts
Build deterministic tests that cover mathematical behavior, edge cases, and input immutability
Analyze convergence behavior and the time and space costs of the implementation

in_scope: A reusable Python component and deterministic tests
out_of_scope: Completion of the Coursera specialization or any constituent course
Reproduction of an official Coursera assignment
Logistic regression and later machine-learning topics

unit_completion_requires: All four learner deliverables are present
The worker-harness-controlled test command completes successfully
The independent examiner records sufficient rubric evidence
No critical rubric condition is triggered
completion_policy.evidence_policy: Learner or worker prose is not completion evidence; promotion requires validator-controlled evidence recorded by the worker harness.
completion_policy.after_unit_completion: Mark only this manager-authored kickoff unit complete. Keep the course status partial until separately sourced, prepared, attempted, and validated units satisfy a future whole-course policy.

provenance.selection_basis: The catalog description explicitly names linear regression and hands-on programming; the software-engineering requirements, API, tests, questions, and rubric were authored for this bounded kickoff.
provenance.retrieval: No linked, authenticated, paywalled, recording, assignment, or textbook content was fetched or copied.
